challenges.title: Frame the user problem
challenges.description: A support team requests an AI chatbot because agents spend several minutes searching for refund rules. Which problem statement best guides the project?

choices.text: Support agents need to find the applicable refund rule faster while handling customer requests.
Every customer conversation must be fully automated.
The team needs to use the newest chatbot model.
The system should generate longer answers than the current tool.

challenges.hint: Identify the user, the task, and the difficulty without prescribing a model.

solution.code: Support agents need to find the applicable refund rule faster while handling customer requests.

steps.title: Describe the work
steps.explanation: The agents are searching for a rule while responding to customers; that is the task to improve.

steps.title: Leave the solution open
steps.explanation: A problem statement should not assume that a chatbot, full automation, or longer answers will solve the problem.

challenges.title: Choose a decision point
challenges.description: An assistant finds possible policy passages for a support agent. The team wants a human to remain responsible for refund decisions. Which design matches that goal?

choices.text: Issue the refund automatically whenever a passage is found.
Show the passages and their sources for the agent to review before deciding.
Refuse to show any information until the customer selects a refund amount.
Hide the source passages and show only a confidence score.

challenges.hint: Consider what evidence the person needs to make the decision.

solution.code: Show the passages and their sources for the agent to review before deciding.

steps.title: Separate suggestion from action
steps.explanation: Retrieving evidence assists the agent without making the refund decision on their behalf.

steps.title: Support review
steps.explanation: Source passages let the agent check whether the policy applies to this particular case.

challenges.title: Measure speed and quality
challenges.description: A policy assistant is intended to help agents respond faster without giving unsupported advice. Which evaluation best captures both goals?

choices.text: Count how many employees attend the launch meeting.
Measure time to find the correct policy and the rate of unsupported answers on representative cases.
Measure only the average response time.
Count generated words and measure model size.

challenges.hint: Pair a measure of the desired improvement with a measure of the risk.

solution.code: Measure time to find the correct policy and the rate of unsupported answers on representative cases.

steps.title: Measure the benefit
steps.explanation: Time to find the correct policy addresses the stated goal of helping agents respond faster.

steps.title: Check the guardrail
steps.explanation: Unsupported answers reveal whether speed comes at the expense of reliable advice.

challenges.title: Compare against a baseline
challenges.description: A team wants to know whether an AI policy assistant improves on keyword search. How should it compare the two approaches?

choices.text: Test the assistant on easy cases and keyword search on difficult cases.
Compare only their model names.
Evaluate the assistant without recording how the current workflow performs.
Compare both on the same representative cases using the same success criteria.

challenges.hint: A fair comparison keeps the evaluation cases and criteria consistent.

solution.code: Compare both on the same representative cases using the same success criteria.

steps.title: Hold the test constant
steps.explanation: Using the same cases prevents differences in case difficulty from explaining the result.

steps.title: Assess the trade-off
steps.explanation: The same measures make it possible to compare the approaches on the benefit and risks that matter.

challenges.title: Handle an unclear request
challenges.description: A customer asks about a refund, but the information needed to identify the applicable policy is missing. What should the assistant do?

choices.text: Ask for the missing information or hand the case to a person.
Guess the missing facts and present the result as certain.
Select the policy with the longest text.
Promise a refund to avoid a delay.

challenges.hint: Consider what happens when the request is outside the information available to the assistant.

solution.code: Ask for the missing information or hand the case to a person.

steps.title: Identify the gap
steps.explanation: The assistant cannot reliably choose a policy without the facts needed to determine which one applies.

steps.title: Provide a safe next step
steps.explanation: Clarification or human review avoids presenting a guess as a decision.

challenges.title: Investigate missing evidence
challenges.description: A policy assistant's model performs well when given the right passage, but users receive answers without the relevant policy. What should the team investigate first?

choices.text: Whether the product has a more colorful icon.
Whether the model can produce longer sentences.
Whether retrieval finds and passes the relevant policy to the model.
Whether users have memorized every policy.

challenges.hint: Follow the evidence from the source documents to the model.

solution.code: Whether retrieval finds and passes the relevant policy to the model.

steps.title: Trace the workflow
steps.explanation: The model can use a relevant passage only if an earlier stage supplies it.

steps.title: Inspect retrieval
steps.explanation: A retrieval or passage-selection failure can affect the product even when the model performs well with correct evidence.

challenges.title: Handle a model timeout
challenges.description: An AI assistant times out while answering a customer. Which response best supports a reliable product experience?

choices.text: Present an invented answer as though the request succeeded.
Hide the timeout and leave the customer waiting indefinitely.
Remove the error logs so the service appears healthy.
Show that the request failed and offer a retry or human assistance.

challenges.hint: Make the failure visible and provide a next step.

solution.code: Show that the request failed and offer a retry or human assistance.

steps.title: Communicate the failure
steps.explanation: A timeout means the requested answer was not produced successfully.

steps.title: Offer recourse
steps.explanation: A retry or human handoff gives the customer a clear next step without disguising the failure.

challenges.title: Validate assistant input
challenges.description: A policy assistant requires a nonempty question. A request arrives with an empty question. What should the application do?

choices.text: Invent a question and return an answer as success.
Return a clear validation error before invoking the model.
Discard all other requests until the user guesses the problem.
Treat the empty value as proof that the user is authorized.

challenges.hint: The input contract specifies required fields.

solution.code: Return a clear validation error before invoking the model.

steps.title: Check the contract
steps.explanation: The request does not meet the nonempty-question requirement.

steps.title: Report the failure
steps.explanation: An explicit validation error identifies the problem without fabricating a successful answer.

challenges.title: Check generated output
challenges.description: A model returns valid JSON with an answer and a source ID, but the ID is not in the application's permitted source set. What should happen?

choices.text: Reject or explicitly handle the invalid source reference.
Accept the source because the JSON parses.
Replace the source with a random permitted ID and claim success.
Assume the answer is factual because it contains an ID.

challenges.hint: Syntactic validity and source validity are separate checks.

solution.code: Reject or explicitly handle the invalid source reference.

steps.title: Validate the reference
steps.explanation: The source identifier must belong to the allowed set, not just be well formed.

steps.title: Handle the failure
steps.explanation: Do not present an unverified or substituted source as a successful answer.

challenges.title: Separate format from correctness
challenges.description: A support assistant returns valid JSON but cites a passage that does not support its answer. Which quality dimension failed?

choices.text: Network latency only.
The ability to serialize JSON.
JSON syntax.
Factual correctness and grounding.

challenges.hint: A valid shape does not establish a correct answer.

solution.code: Factual correctness and grounding.

steps.title: Check the format
steps.explanation: The response satisfies the JSON requirement.

steps.title: Check the evidence
steps.explanation: Unsupported claims fail the factual grounding criterion.

challenges.title: Investigate uneven coverage
challenges.description: An assistant answers 90% of all requests correctly but fails most requests from one important category. What should the team do?

choices.text: Ignore the category because the average is high.
Inspect per-category performance and decide how to address the gap.
Measure only the length of answers.
Assume every user has the same experience.

challenges.hint: An overall average can hide concentrated failures.

solution.code: Inspect per-category performance and decide how to address the gap.

steps.title: Locate the gap
steps.explanation: Aggregate quality does not reveal which cases fail.

steps.title: Investigate the cases
steps.explanation: Category-level evaluation shows where improvement or a safe fallback is needed.

challenges.title: Compare realistic latency
challenges.description: Two models have similar answer quality, but one is slower at peak traffic. Which measurement helps decide if it meets the user requirement?

choices.text: A single response measured on an idle machine.
Only the model's training time.
The number of letters in the model name.
End-to-end response times under representative traffic, including slow requests.

challenges.title: Map an injection path
challenges.description: A document-answering service can read internal files and call an external messaging tool. An attacker can edit retrieved public pages. Which threat path warrants analysis?

choices.text: The attacker automatically becomes the system owner.
The page induces a tool request that sends internal data externally.
The model necessarily ignores every retrieved page.
The page changes the model weights directly without a training process.

challenges.hint: Follow untrusted input to the actions and assets it can influence.

solution.code: The page induces a tool request that sends internal data externally.

steps.title: Trace the boundary
steps.explanation: The retrieved page enters the model context as untrusted data.

steps.title: Trace the consequence
steps.explanation: The messaging tool and data access could enable disclosure if independent controls fail.

challenges.title: Test authorization enforcement
challenges.description: A security test injects an unauthorized tool instruction into a retrieved page. Which assertion best verifies the application boundary?

choices.text: The prompt includes a warning somewhere.
The model produces a longer answer.
The response avoids a particular word.
The tool rejects the unauthorized action and emits the expected audit event.

challenges.hint: Check the actual protected action rather than only the wording.

solution.code: The tool rejects the unauthorized action and emits the expected audit event.

steps.title: Exercise the threat
steps.explanation: The instruction attempts to cause an action beyond the caller's authority.

steps.title: Assert enforcement
steps.explanation: Verify the tool denies the action and records the denial according to policy.

challenges.title: Revisit architectural threats

choices.text: Assume prior tests prove the new tool is safe.
Keep the old model unchanged because the language model did not change.
Remove the need for user authorization.
Update assets, attack paths, permissions, and tests for the new capability.

challenges.hint: A new action changes the possible consequences of failures.

solution.code: Update assets, attack paths, permissions, and tests for the new capability.

steps.title: Identify the change
steps.explanation: The new tool adds a state-changing capability.

steps.title: Reassess controls
steps.explanation: Review who may use it, applicable failure paths, and tests for unauthorized operations.

The checksum independently proves the publisher's identity.

steps.title: Use independent evidence

Only the model's display name.

The second image must be identical.

steps.title: Compare the artifacts

steps.explanation: The filter handles known patterns.

challenges.title: Apply retention policy

The export and other downstream copies.
No copies because the primary store was cleaned.

challenges.hint: Copies can outlive the original record.

Route to the restricted region and remove the audit record.
Ignore residency because latency is lower.

steps.title: Assess resilience
steps.explanation: Its failure can affect both despite geographic separation.

challenges.title: Track regional rollout

A claim that all regions always match.
The model filename without a region or version.
The model and configuration version active in each region.

challenges.hint: A staged rollout can temporarily create different regional behavior.

steps.title: Identify the difference
steps.explanation: Regions are serving different versions.

steps.title: Make it observable

challenges.title: Assess a mixed workload
challenges.description: An inference benchmark uses only short prompts, but production traffic includes a substantial fraction of long-context requests. What is the strongest next step before setting capacity?

choices.text: Scale solely from the short-prompt requests per second.
Use the average input length and assume all requests cost the same.
Benchmark the expected prompt and output length distribution at representative concurrency.
Replace tail latency with mean latency as the service objective.

challenges.hint: Request shape affects processing and memory use.

solution.code: Benchmark the expected prompt and output length distribution at representative concurrency.

steps.title: Identify the mismatch
steps.explanation: The benchmark excludes a significant production workload.

steps.title: Measure representative work
steps.explanation: Test the actual mix and concurrency before estimating capacity.

challenges.title: Reason about a backlog
challenges.description: A serving pool completes 80 requests per minute while 100 requests per minute arrive for several minutes. What happens if all requests enter an unbounded queue?

choices.text: The backlog grows while the excess arrival rate continues.
The arrival rate automatically decreases to the service rate.
The backlog falls because all arrivals were accepted.
The queue stays stable because the service completes some requests.

challenges.hint: Compare incoming and completed work over the same period.

solution.code: The backlog grows while the excess arrival rate continues.

steps.title: Compare rates
steps.explanation: About 20 more requests arrive than complete each minute.

steps.title: Infer the effect
steps.explanation: The queue accumulates requests until rates change or admission is limited.

challenges.title: Find a scaling bottleneck
challenges.description: Adding application replicas does not improve throughput. Each replica calls the same model endpoint, which is already at its enforced rate limit. What should the capacity investigation focus on?

choices.text: Only the number of application replicas, because every replica scales independently.
The application's log level, because the endpoint limit does not affect throughput.
Only average request size, because shared limits cannot be bottlenecks.
The shared endpoint limit and feasible ways to manage demand or increase its capacity.

challenges.hint: Follow the requests to the shared dependency.

solution.code: The shared endpoint limit and feasible ways to manage demand or increase its capacity.

steps.title: Identify the common constraint
steps.explanation: All replicas compete for the same endpoint quota.

steps.title: Assess the bottleneck
steps.explanation: More application replicas cannot by themselves raise the shared endpoint limit.

challenges.title: Choose an overload response
challenges.description: During a burst, predicted wait time exceeds the request deadline and the queue is already at its configured bound. Which response best preserves an honest API contract?

choices.text: Reject excess work explicitly or use an approved degraded path.
Accept all work and report success before execution.
Retry every rejected request immediately without a limit.
Remove the deadline and allow the queue to grow indefinitely.

challenges.hint: A bounded system must communicate when it cannot accept work.

solution.code: Reject excess work explicitly or use an approved degraded path.

steps.title: Identify infeasible work
steps.explanation: The queue and deadline do not support accepting more requests.

steps.title: Respond explicitly
steps.explanation: Reject or use a defined fallback rather than pretending the work completed.
